An aqueduct-city channeling underground rivers through carved obsidian channels across a vast cavern ceiling, the sound of dark water a constant pressure, noble houses clustered along the highest flows.

A colosseum of black granite where Houses settle disputes through ritual combat, galleries carved to hold ten thousand observers, the fighting pit inlaid with spider-silk patterns in contrasting pale stone.

A fungal-garden district of cultivated darkness, enormous cave-mushrooms tended by slaves in lightless passages, the drow overseers moving by echolocation alone, architecture minimal and brutal in its sufficiency.
A prison-spire of seamless black obsidian descending below city level rather than rising, each cell carved smaller than the last as depth increases, the lowest chamber a single sealed cube of stone.
A drow noble's private sanctum cut into a crystal geode, the raw amethyst walls left unfinished on one side and polished to black mirrors on the other, furnished entirely in carved bone.

A harbor-cavern for subterranean river-boats, stone quays of obsidian descending into black water, moored vessels of dark wood loaded with slaves and poison, faerie-fire torches reflected in oily ripples.

A grand boulevard carved through solid rock two hundred feet wide, lined with obsidian columns bearing the names of conquered surface-world cities, terminating at a sealed gate carved in the shape of a scream.

A necropolis district of carved burial-niches descending into cavern floor, noble houses interred in obsidian sarcophagi within chambers sealed with spider-silk and faerie-fire, the architecture more refined than the city of the living above.

A watchtower-cluster of seven black spires at the cavern perimeter, each connected by enclosed bridge-tunnels, manned by crossbow-armed drow who have not seen another face in years, their architecture of total vigilance.

The matriarch's palace at the absolute city center, a structure of such age its obsidian walls have begun to crystallize, every surface carved with a history of betrayal, its deepest room never opened.

A vertical city descending a mile-deep chasm in carved obsidian tiers, each level connected by spider-silk bridges trembling over nothing, faerie-fire tracing the strata like cold violet veins in living rock.
An obsidian palace mirrored perfectly in a subterranean lake of black water, so that the real towers and their reflections form one seamless dark architecture, indistinguishable above and below.
